sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Kumar Kulshrestha Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Deepak Kumar Kulshrestha, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ashutosh Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No. 110 of 2023, registered under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 120-B I.P.C. at Police Station- Sunil Verma vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175619100/

entities.text: Police Station- Sunil Verma vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Kamla Nagar, District- Agra with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
4. As per prosecution story, the named accused person Lala Lalwani is stated to have taken golden loan worth Rs. 1,40,000/- from the company of the informant on 2.9.2022.
It was found later on that the said golden bracelet was fake.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is not named in the FIR and his name has come up later on in the statement of arrested co-accused persons, which is not admissible in evidence.
The applicant has no criminal history to his credit.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

9. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
